h1: What winery consultancy covers, from grapes to bottle
title: What Winery Consultancy Covers | Craft Beer School
desc: What a winery consultant does from vineyard intake to bottled wine: site, equipment, process, quality, costing and licensing. A guide for owners.
teaser: A winery is a food factory with a harvest deadline. Consultancy should cover the whole path, not just the cellar.
standfirst: Winery consultancy runs from the grapes at the gate to the wine in the bottle. This guide lists the parts of that path, so you can see what support you need and what to ask for.
sections:
Grapes arrive in a short window, get processed in days and then spend months in the cellar. Mistakes at the start show up at bottling. A consultant who looks only at the cellar misses half the picture.

We structure winery work along the actual flow of the product, from intake to packaging. We add the business side where owners need it.

Planning comes first. This means choosing capacity from realistic grape supply, deciding between tank and barrel capacity and laying out the hall so grapes, must, wine and waste do not cross paths.

Equipment choice is part of this: destemmer and crusher, press, tanks with temperature control, pumps, filtration and the bottling line. Over-buying is common in new wineries. Buying too little capacity for harvest week is the other mistake. Both are expensive.

Process support covers decisions that determine the wine. Picking date, sugar and acid targets, sulphur additions, yeast choice, fermentation temperature and the choice between skin contact and quick pressing all belong here.

Red wine takes its colour from skins during fermentation. White wine is normally pressed before fermenting and kept cool to hold fruit character. These choices need to match the grapes you actually have. Conditions in warm regions change ripening and acid. A process copied from a cool climate may not fit.

We write process sheets a cellar team can follow, with the numbers to check at each step.

A winery needs a basic laboratory routine: sugar, pH, total acidity, free and total sulphur dioxide and volatile acidity. Measured regularly, these catch trouble early. Ankur Napa leads on setting up quality systems and the records behind them.

Stability work covers clarifying, cold stabilisation where needed, filtration and the step before bottling. Bottling itself is where oxygen pick-up and dirty lines undo months of work. We help set procedures for cleaning, filling and closure checks.

Many first-time owners know the price of grapes and not the cost of a bottle. Costing adds labour, utilities, barrels, bottles, closures, labels, losses and overheads, then asks what the wine must sell for. See our guide on what goes into a project report for how these numbers fit into a business case.

We can also support product planning, so the range you launch matches the grapes you can source and the customers you can reach.

In India alcohol is a state subject. Licences, excise rules and some label requirements differ from state to state and change. We describe the steps, but you should work with a licensing adviser or lawyer in your state and check the current notification.

The work runs remotely by video call and shared data, with site visits by arrangement, ideally around harvest. We start with a review of your plan or your winery as it stands, give you a written action plan and support the parts you choose. We do not promise outcomes or quote fees in advance of understanding your project.
Harvest week and what to prepare

Harvest compresses the year into a few weeks. Before the first truck arrives, check that every pump, hose and press runs, that tanks are clean and cooled, that the laboratory has fresh reagents and that people know their roles.

Write down the receiving routine: weighing, sampling for sugar and acid, sorting. Then say where each lot goes. Mix-ups at intake are hard to trace later. A one-page plan stuck to the wall beats a clever plan that lives in someone's head.

We help build this checklist before harvest and, by arrangement, join the team on site or by video call while the first lots are processed.

Keep a harvest diary too. Note dates, sugar readings, weather and what you did. Next year it becomes the most useful document in the winery, because the grapes will behave differently and you will want something to compare against.

If you have never run a harvest, our Winemaking course gives the team a shared vocabulary before the first lot arrives.
faqs: Can you help before I have bought land or equipment?
Yes. That is the best time. Capacity, equipment and layout decisions are cheaper to correct on paper.
We advise and support the team you have or hire. We can help define the roles and the skills needed. We can also train people on the process.
We explain the process and help you prepare documents. The licence itself comes from your state authority. A licensing adviser or lawyer should guide that step.
